'''Chunming Zhang''' is a Chinese and American statistician whose research involves [[nonparametric statistics]] and [[semiparametric model]]s with applications including [[neuroscience]] and [[statistical finance]]. She is a professor of statistics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]],{{r|profile}} and the chair of the Nonparametric Statistics Section of the [[American Statistical Association]].{{r|nss}}

==Education and career==
Zhang was an undergraduate at [[Nankai University]], and earned a master's degree through the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].{{r|bio}} She completed a Ph.D. at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 2000. Her dissertation, ''Topics in the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test'', was supervised by [[Jianqing Fan]].{{r|mg}}

She joined the University of Wisconsin–Madison as an assistant professor in 2000, and has been a full professor since 2010.{{r|bio}}

==Recognition==
Zhang was elected as a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2011, "for influential contributions to theory and methodology for high-dimensional data, for unifying common loss functions through Bregman divergence, and for fundamental work in nonparametric and semiparametric methodology together with applications in multiple testing, brain-imaging and finance".{{r|fims}}

She became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2016.{{r|fasa}} She is a 2024 Medallion Lecturer of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.{{r|medallion}}
